results.title: How Much Does It Cost To Rent An NVIDIA GPU?
results.author: Alec Pow
highlights:
Published on September 18, 2026 | Researched and reviewed by Alec Pow, Founder & Pricing Investigator Prices, claims, and calculations checked against 12 cited sources. See our research methodology and corrections policy.

...

B200 capacity can reach $6.79 to $12.355 per GPU-hour. The hourly rate is only one part of the bill. A machine that stays provisioned while idle, persistent storage, multi-GPU minimums and interruptible-capacity rules can change the real cost more than a small difference in sticker rate.

...

Higher-memory data-center GPUs move into a different price band. RunPod’s September 2026 pricing lists Secure Cloud rates of $0.74 per hour for RTX 4090, $0.99 for RTX 5090, $1.59 for A100, $2.89 for H100 PCIe, $4.59 for H200 and $6.79 for B200. Lambda’s self-service pricing lists a single H100 PCIe at $3.29 per GPU-hour and a single B200 at $6.99.

| GPU | Provider example | Published rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V100 16GB | CloudRift | $0.25/hr |
| RTX 4090 24GB | CloudRift | $0.39/hr |
| RTX 5090 32GB | CloudRift | $0.60/hr |
| A100 80GB | CloudRift | $1.05/hr |
| H100 80GB | Spheron | $2.64/hr |
| H100 PCIe 80GB | RunPod Secure | $2.89/hr |
| H100 PCIe 80GB | Lambda | $3.29/hr |
| H100 80GB | DigitalOcean | $4.41/hr |
| H100 80GB | Paperspace | $5.95/hr |
| B200 180GB | RunPod Secure | $6.79/hr |
| B200 180GB | Lambda | $6.99/hr |
| B200 | AWS Capacity Block | $12.355/GPU-hr |

...

A GPU-hour is one accelerator allocated for one hour, but one GPU-hour does not buy the same amount of memory or throughput across models. NVIDIA’s HGX hardware specifications list 80GB of HBM3 on H100 SXM, 141GB of HBM3e on H200 and 180GB of HBM3e on B200. Memory bandwidth rises from 3.35 TB/s on H100 to 4.8 TB/s on H200 and up to 8 TB/s on B200. That extra memory can determine whether a large model fits on one GPU at all.

...

Another H100 example is Paperspace at $5.95 per hour. AWS Capacity Blocks price a U.S. H100 accelerator at $5.191 per accelerator-hour, while a B200 accelerator is $12.355. Capacity Blocks are reservation products rather than ordinary minute-by-minute marketplace capacity.

The price difference can exceed twofold before performance is considered. A 100-hour H100 job would cost $264 at the Spheron example, $441 at DigitalOcean, $519.10 at the U.S. AWS Capacity Block rate or $595 at Paperspace. Those totals do not prove that the lowest number is the best value. Availability, H100 variant, host RAM, network fabric, storage, support and reservation rules can all change which service is usable for the job.

...

- Checked an independent September cloud GPU index, which places the current H100 on-demand range at $2.47 to $12.29 per GPU-hour.
- Cross-referenced the September GPU rental index, which reports a $3.25 per GPU-hour H100 median and $4.40 H200 median.
- Verified current market-price movement, including Nebius announcing 17% to 21% increases on selected pay-as-you-go NVIDIA GPU rates effective October 1, 2026.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Published Sep 17, 2026, 09:47 AM

© Reuters

Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: Nebius raises on-demand GPU prices from 1 October | VETTDD
results.author: Editor Editorial desk, VETTDD
highlights:
The neocloud’s published price list lifts H100, H200, B200 and B300 hourly rates by 17–21%, and partners reselling AI compute are likely to need to rebase their quotes

...

The facts

- Spot prices for preemptible HGX H100 and H200 instances start from $0.79 (£0.60) per GPU-hour, and Nebius says they can change as often as every 15 minutes.
- Nebius’s pricing FAQ gives US dollars as the only currency it accepts.
- Egress and ingress traffic, public IP addresses and Nebius’s managed Kubernetes service are listed as free.

...

Nebius will charge more for on-demand graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity from 1 October 2026, according to the price list on its website. An Nvidia HGX H100 instance rises from $3.85 (£2.91) to $4.50 (£3.40) per GPU-hour, and an HGX B300 from $7.85 (£5.93) to $9.50 (£7.17).

The rest of the HGX range moves the same way. H200 goes from $4.50 to $5.40 (£4.08) and B200 from $7.15 (£5.40) to $8.50 (£6.42). On the page’s own figures, the four rises run from 17% to 21%. Central processing unit (CPU) instances go up too, with AMD Epyc Genoa starting at $0.13 (£0.10) an hour instead of $0.10. RTX Pro 6000 and L40S prices are unchanged, and the rack-scale GB300 and GB200 NVL72 systems remain price on request.
